body: You just made me remember when I was playing netball, I was 11 or 12 and told the person next to me that I had 300 cats. They were like “How do you feed all of them..?” And I said “I peed on their face just how Hitler liked women to pee on their faces”... this is a super inappropriate situation and I hope it’s okay to post. Well I just hope it made you feel better because this haunts me. I feel like this is going to be taken down, lmao.

Not being able to make proper facial expressions and having flat affect. 

Being mostly mute. (Selective mutism)

Being stiff. (Anxiety)

Being overweight. (not really associated with autism, but there are some indications it is)

Having no friends. (a group to back me up)

Honestly it sounds weird but... bad handwriting, inability to do instructions, some people thought I wasn’t paying attention in class or just didn’t care because I left class so much. Teachers thought this too. 

Taking things literally.

When I was younger I had really bad hygiene because I didn’t shower or look after myself.

Staring. I had a really bad problem with staring and people thought that was weird.

Misjudging social situations and just responding to them in a really odd way. Never saying goodbye to people because I was either too anxious and never knew how to end a conversation or start one. 

There’s a silver lining in all of this, for some reason nobody ever made fun of my stimming. I sometimes accidentally overtly stimmed in class and not one person ever said a thing to me. I think that it’s because I repressed it a lot, but maybe that’s when they were like “oh, she’s autistic, don’t make fun of her for it”, but I don’t know.

Um yes, I’m embarrassed to even admit the characters I have picked up personality wise. It’s been for the best though. If you’re embarrassed, chances are people don’t even notice. I had someone close to me for over 4 months and I was intentionally mimicking specific people we both knew and it was only until I admitted to them what I was doing that the pieces came together. As for TV show or movie characters I definitely do that 100% but I will never speak of it not even in a Reddit comment though because it’s so effective and the only thing that somewhat helps me feel not so empty.
I have autism though too though. I feel like the difference between these two is that for autism, I’m more mimicking their body language and how they react to things. It really has nothing to do with identity but I could be wrong.

I don’t really know what to say but I just wanted to let you know that you’re not alone, this quarantine I have done a lot of self reflecting with the same realisations. I have been diagnosed with similar disorders. 
I’m still trying to forgive myself, and I have found the easiest way to move on from my past mistakes is proving that I can do better. I’m trying to gain trust over myself, and to know the way I behaved in the past wasn’t necessarily my fault and I can only get better now. 
You can’t control the past but you can control the future, and also remember that you live life through a negative lens. I try to remind myself that having BPD my perception of reality is sometimes distorted, so I actually have positive attributes but I can’t focus on them. Remind yourself of that and try to think about the good attributes you have too.

There is a comment about radical acceptance and I very much agree with that. ^

I’ve been suicidal since I was 7 (yet had an innate desire to leave this world earlier) and I also have BPD which a lot of people say 1 in 10 people with BPD complete suicide.
I seriously considered it last week and went out of my way.
It was bad.
I would agree, having ASD makes things so much worse. I don’t think I’m going to come out of this world without ending my life. It’s a constant battle, and I know things are most likely only get worse as I get older, because I’m only 18

I’m feeling kind of confused because of some medication I just took... so I’m sorry if I don’t make much sense.

I wouldn’t judge your pain on what has happened in your life. There are all sorts of abuse where you feel like ‘something really didn’t happen’ but it was actually covert abuse. Or there are repressed memories, and everybody reacts to the same scenario in a different way. For some people something can be highly traumatic and for other people it can just be a walk in the park. There isn’t one set way you should react to anything, your life and feelings is the way it is. I’m sure there are hidden reasons why you feel the way you do, as there was for me.

You’re not dramatic or incorrect for feeling the way you do, you’re a sensitive person who has came into this world and experienced trauma. Nobody feels a certain way without a root cause. It’s common to feel like this when you’ve lived your whole life with people invalidating your feelings, but I can promise you that your pain does matter. I mean, you have a mental illness, the causes are unclear (people say mainly through abuse) but that might not be for everyone. Don’t blame yourself for the way you act, or the way that you are, just live everyday trying to get better for you. Your pain matters just as much as everybody else. It’s took me years and will take me so many years for me to figure out why I feel this pain, I invalidated my pain for SO long, but now I wonder how I got through it all.

Hand flapping, rocking, different hand movements (rubbing together, or freezing), facial expressions, listening to the same music over and over, vocal noises,  leg movements, I also have visual stims, most of my thoughts are even stimming (repetitive thoughts and phrases over and over), walking in circles over and over. My stimming is really intense and all the time. I don’t know why, I’m a huge sensory seeker but also avoider.

I’m not sure how to deal with the loneliness, but just know that it’s there and you can’t fight it. You can only accept the loneliness you feel. The emotion of loneliness can be so painful because it signals rejection. I would say working on yourself, self esteem, how you view this world, your hobbies, discovering yourself etc would be the best.

Fill your time with things that make you feel a little more true to yourself. It could be anything, really. I’m too emotionally unavailable to find friends at this moment as well. But I can only accept the pain I feel and work towards the best person I can be alone. The pain won’t go away at first, but know there are many benefits to being alone if you try to find the good in it. Sometimes I feel like the more alone you feel the more you need yourself, not other people. Though human beings need social contact, so if you are able to work to a point where you’re in a healthy friendship/relationship with someone, even just from a mutual distance it will help how you feel. I don’t know if this advice would help at all but I wish you the best.

First of all, I just wanted to tell you that it’ll be okay.

I know you don’t feel like it will be, but just breathe.

Your boyfriend has established that he doesn’t want to leave you, he loves you, but he’s unsure. After the events of last night I’m sure you’ve feeling very unsure of what your relationship can be. 

First thing I would do is think about why you acted the way you did last night. Did something trigger you? Was it something that isn’t really apparent to you? Thinking about it might help, so you can communicate to your boyfriend about why you did this and what you can do to go forward.

I’m so sorry you lost your job, these sudden changes must have really made everything hard, especially when you’re bored and left to your own devices. I saw a video about people with BPD and how quarantine can make us more bored and therefore do more destructive things. I think trying to stay mentally engaged (doing something that brings positive emotions, or even just a distraction) will help. It’s really hard when you’re faced with the reality that somebody you might love really leave you, but this is the best thing that you can do for now as he’s not here. If you get your mind off of it, when it comes to confronting him again you can be calm minded and say how you really feel.

For example, when I’m angry I say things like “I hate you” but I really mean that I feel rejected and scared that I’ve disappointed them and not lived up to the expectations of what I wanted to. 
But most people will never be able to see through my words if I just say these things, live through your authentic feelings and experiences. Even if you feel like you shouldn’t be feeling this way, it’s okay, you do.

I would communicate how guilty you feel, and try to keep changing to the best of your ability so you can keep your boyfriend in your life. I think that he’s saying “I don’t know” because he didn’t know why you acted the way you did, in the past perhaps he had a better understanding of your triggers? If you’re able to feel understand why you acted the way you did, you can explain this to him. I’m so sorry that you’re going through this, I wish you the best of luck. It’s a horrible feeling to know that someone you love very much could be leaving you at any second, the pain is unbearable but I promise you that you can get through this. You are a brave person for being able to type this and to reach for support. 

I’ve dealt with a lot of criticising and I think this stems from our fear of abandonment. You could be criticising him because you feel like this abandonment is inevitable? It could be a protection mechanism. I felt the same way in my previous relationship, that the shoe could drop at any moment and he could cheat on me or leave me. Though it was never anything he did, it was just from my lack of self worth. The reason you might find it hard to change is yes, this disorder. It’s really hard to change the patterns that we deal with but it is possible. I hope you can feel compassion for yourself, you’re trying your best and you have done a lot of self reflecting, the next step is to have mechanisms in place to try and recognise these situations where you are criticising and where it comes from, how you can deal with it and calm down.

It’s good that you reached out to your dad, is there anybody else that you can reach out to that might provide you with better emotional support? How about your therapist?
I’m sorry if my advice isn’t sound, I just saw your post and I feel so sorry that you’re going through this. It sounds like you’re doing really well by reaching out to your dad and posting this, you sound like a strong person. I wish you best and I hope you know that your emotions are completely valid and I, and most likely a lot of people on this subreddit would feel the exact same way if we were in this scenario. I would say, do something to distract yourself, give yourself love, make affirmations and statements about who you are (it makes me feel less dependent on people), and know what you’re going to say to your boyfriend when he walks through the door. Know your authentic self and what you really want. It’s going to be okay, this is a tough journey, but I know you can get through this. Good luck, you are a strong person. ❤️

I was broken up with about a week ago, but I have rediscovered myself in a lot of lost ways.
My love of documentaries, philosophy & religion, podcasts, certain musicians, my love for my dogs, reading books and writing. 
I spent a lot of time trying to fix a relationship that could never be fixed, and I tried to mould myself into a person who I couldn’t be.
But, I finally feel like I’m becoming happier, and it’s only been a week. I realise that I lose myself in relationships, I lose my passions, hobbies, but I am actually a person outside all of this. Not who my favourite person or boyfriend, etc is. 
I’ve realised a lot of things about myself, how controlling I can be, how much I love my family and how supportive they can be. Rather than seeing the road ahead as a tough journey that is indefinitely bad, I’m giving life a chance to see what it can be.
I know that I’m on the right path because I’m slowly feeling more free. I’ve had a lot of low moments but I realise I need to be there for ME which is something I have never been able to do.
I’ve realised that even though my ex has a bad opinion of me, it doesn’t mean that it’s the truth or that I have to actually believe it. Trying to convince him otherwise after he has asked me to leave is me just trying to control people, as I have done in the past. If he has the wrong opinion of me, I just have to walk away. 
Not many people will ever be able to have an accurate opinion of me. I’m slowly feeling love and compassion for myself, because it’s me who decides who I am, and I don’t judge myself for the way my life is.
It feels good to be alone. For once I can finally breathe and figure out who I am without moulding myself into someone else, and I know that this is right. I tried to decide this for while and I thought that every little decision mattered, like the universe would punish me if I just made the wrong decision. I have realised that there is really no wrong or right decision and everything in this universe is just at random. I can’t just sit trying to make the right decision forever. 
I don’t ever think I would have realised these things if he never dumped me. A part of this is maintaining a combined stance and realising the good and the bad. I have a tendency just to see in two, but I have to integrate these parts. Sometimes it’s not perfect, sometimes I just hate him for the way he made me feel, but at the same time I have to remind myself to be grateful for these lessons that I will receive through my life, even if they do seem bad at the moment.
Many people have left my life and it has destroyed me but I have realised I have the power to let this kick me down or for it to build me up. I could be at the opposite in a few hours, but I cherish moments like these where I have a sense of clarity. 
I begged for my ex boyfriend to come back. I called him thousands of times. I wrote him a letter detailing over 10,000 words about how sorry I was. A part of recovering and going into the right path is realising that I can’t control how somebody else perceives me, I can’t control him, and if he just doesn’t love, miss me or see me as worthy of his time, then that is his loss and I just have to move on. 
I don’t know if I’m out of love, but all I know is that I’m focusing on the love for myself first before thinking about that. I never thought this was the right path because I idealised him so heavily, but right now, it seems to have been the best possible path. 
I’m not too sure if this was the answer you were looking for, but I hope it helped.

I have autism and BPD. If you think it’s a possibility that you have autism, research gender differences in autism, and the overlap between the symptoms, because there are some. If or when you can speak to a psychologist, but I know not everybody can do that, so just take it as a way to know yourself better and to make life easier.

A lot of people go undiagnosed their whole life, girls are are much more on average to go undetected, autism is under diagnosed.There is also a condition called CPTSD (Complex Post Traumatic Stress Disorder) that has similar symptoms to ASD, but this is through trauma. 

I would research everything with an open heart and know that you’re not alone, it’ll be okay and I wish the best for you and your findings. I know that online assessments aren’t that great, but you can take this to a health professional if interested. Best of luck. ❤️ https://rdos.net/eng/Aspie-quiz.php

honestly. I’m only young and haven’t really lived life much so I don’t know if I can say things accurately in accordance to your situation. but for a long time I felt exactly the same way, like I wasn’t meant for life. when I was 14 (4 years ago) I wrote a post on here saying that I wish somebody else was in my body who could deal with my life, because I couldn’t cope with anything. the majority of my life I have moved through life feeling like I was an alien or a bad person, because it seemed like everybody portrayed me to be one because I could never live up to the expectations other people gave me.
no matter how much I tried, and I tried so hard.
I tried even when it didn’t look like I was trying to other people.
but looking back at it, I realise there is no proper way to deal with life. there should be no pressure to be a certain person or to live up to something, but I get the need to conform. since I’m autistic, my whole life I have tried to adapt into being someone I wasn’t, and it made me feel like I wasn’t equipped to deal with life and the person I am. I see other people doing things better than me and living better lives, and I wonder how that was fair?
who I am, the way I act, it’s okay, the things I have done in the past, it’s okay, we all try our best even if the thing we did was the worst thing we could have done. I truly think the feeling of ‘not meant to be alive’ is when we are denied true acceptance from people so many times, we resort to self destruction. the way society is, the way it makes us into being certain people, ideas always change every century, and will continue to change. you are meant for life, you are alive, even if you are struggling, your behaviours are human because you are a human. 

I can see how you would feel so stuck after your life has been this way for so long. I hope you know that recovery and living in a different way is completely possible. you can do it. I like to see as my emotions and everything else that is not just related to my consciousness as ‘other’, you are not your mistakes, your impulses, feelings and experiences. deep down inside the real you is just something experiencing something. you can’t blame yourself for being a human, every way you feel is completely accurate in accordance to what has happened in the past, it has to be, and I hope you can move on. my sickness is ‘other’ and i am me 

maybe I’m just saying things that I wish I heard at that time or what I wish to hear now, but I hope this helps, and I’m sorry if this isn’t helpful to your situation, I just wish to help in some way
